# Cold brew extraction log

Started 2026-08-02. Goal: find the ratio and steep time that gives the sweetest, least bitter cold brew from the Ethiopian natural lot, using what I have at home (a scale, a 1 L mason jar, a paper filter setup, and a cheap TDS meter borrowed from Sam).

## Setup
- Coffee: Ethiopia Guji natural, roasted 2026-07-24, ground on coarse (setting 28 on the hand grinder)
- Water: filtered, room temp (about 21 C), fridge at 4 C
- Variables: ratio (1:8, 1:10, 1:12), steep time (12, 16, 20, 24 h), fridge vs counter
- Scoring: my own taste score 1-5 for sweetness / bitterness / body, plus TDS reading

## Runs

| Run | Date | Ratio | Time | Where | TDS % | Sweet | Bitter | Body | Notes |
|-----|------|-------|------|-------|-------|-------|--------|------|-------|
| 1 | 08-02 | 1:10 | 16 h | fridge | 1.31 | 3 | 2 | 3 | clean, a bit thin |
| 2 | 08-04 | 1:8 | 16 h | fridge | 1.74 | 4 | 3 | 4 | strong; good over ice |
| 3 | 08-07 | 1:10 | 24 h | counter | 1.52 | 3 | 4 | 3 | woody edge, too long |
| 4 | 08-09 | 1:10 | 12 h | counter | 1.18 | 3 | 1 | 2 | weak |
| 5 | 08-12 | 1:12 | 20 h | fridge | 1.10 | 2 | 1 | 2 | very mild |
| 6 | 08-15 | 1:8 | 20 h | fridge | 1.92 | 4 | 3 | 5 | best body, a little sharp |

## What I think so far
- Time matters less than ratio between 12 and 20 hours; past 20 h on the counter the bitterness climbs.
- The fridge runs are cleaner than counter runs at the same time. Could be temperature or could be that I stir less. Need to control for stirring.
- Best so far is run 2 or 6; diluting run 6 1:1 with water tasted great (TDS about 0.96 but sweeter than run 5).

## Next
- Try 1:8 at 18 h in fridge, filtered twice
- Same coffee, different grind (setting 24 vs 28)
- Blind taste test with Sam and Lena, 3 cups, scores on cards
